key_insight: The paper shows that a world-action model’s internal representation is crucial for learning effective robot policies: neither pixel-perfect reconstruction nor off-the-shelf perceptual features are enough by themselves. It introduces ReWAM, which makes representation design the central lever for improving both prediction and control.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of choosing a representation space that can support both future observation prediction and robot policy learning in world-action models.
method: Runs controlled comparisons to test which representation properties actually help policy learning.
Builds ReWAM on pre-trained DINO features rather than relying on raw reconstruction objectives.
Adds Feature Calibration and a temporal representation module to better align perception with control and dynamics.
impact: For practitioners, this paper suggests that better robot performance may come from carefully designing the latent representation, not just scaling model size or improving reconstruction loss. It provides a practical direction for building more effective world models for robotics and embodied AI.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing observation -> representation -> action/prediction.
A side-by-side comparison chart of reconstruction-based vs feature-based vs ReWAM representations.
An ablation bar chart showing policy performance under different representation choices.
Icons for vision, memory/temporal dynamics, and robot control to map the model components.
paper_authors: Haoyi Jiang, Liu Liu, Xinjiang Wang, Zhihao Sun, Zequn Chen
